title: Not Just a Sea Breeze
question: What really drives a monsoon, and has it always been the same?
hook: For a long time people explained monsoons as a giant sea breeze, and that explanation has since been dropped.
idea: A monsoon is a seasonal swing in wind and rain tied to the yearly migration of the Intertropical Convergence Zone, and its strength has changed a great deal over Earth's history.

beats.prompt: Land heats up more than the ocean in summer, so an old idea said monsoons were simply a huge sea breeze. What do scientists think now?

choices.label: The sea-breeze idea is right and still the accepted cause
choices.feedback: It sounds sensible, but this explanation is no longer considered the cause.

choices.label: Monsoons follow the yearly migration of the Intertropical Convergence Zone
Monsoons are set off by ocean currents reversing each spring
choices.feedback: Reversing currents are not what sets the monsoon going; the cause is planetary in scale.

choices.label: Monsoons happen only where mountains force air upward
choices.feedback: High ground like the Tibetan Plateau may affect how far north it reaches, but the monsoon itself is planetary in scale.

beats.explain: The sea-breeze idea has been dropped; the monsoon is now treated as a planetary-scale pattern tied to the annual migration of the Intertropical Convergence Zone between its northern and southern limits.

beats.prompt: Put these events in Asia's monsoon history in order.
items: India collides with Asia and the Tibetan Plateau begins to rise
Late Miocene cooling strengthens the East Asian winter monsoon
A widening Tsushima Strait lets the winter monsoon intensify
The East Asian summer monsoon peaks in the Middle Holocene
beats.explain: The collision came around 50 million years ago, the Late Miocene cooling ran from 7.9 to 5.8 million years ago, the Tsushima Strait boost came around 3.8 million years ago, and the summer monsoon peaked around 6,000 years ago.

beats.prompt: Match each term to what it means for monsoons.
pairs: Zone whose yearly migration drives monsoons
Thought to influence how far north the South Asian monsoon reaches
beats.explain: The word came from Arabic through Portuguese, while the convergence zone and the high Tibetan Plateau shape where the monsoon goes.

beats.prompt: Sort each case by what happened to the monsoon.
items: East Asian summer monsoon in interglacials
East Asian summer monsoon at the Last Glacial Maximum
East Asian summer monsoon in Dansgaard–Oeschger events
East Asian summer monsoon in Heinrich events
South American summer monsoon in Dansgaard–Oeschger events
South American summer monsoon in Heinrich events
beats.explain: The same climate swings pushed the East Asian and South American summer monsoons in opposite directions: Dansgaard–Oeschger events strengthened one and weakened the other, and Heinrich events did the reverse.
